scope: Read all 36 passages, overviews, periods, endings, overrides and identity notes. Independently checked selected claims in 11 of 18 sources, including all three writing witnesses. Bounded review, not full historical or border certification.

sourcesChecked.checked: Direct DAI project account: seventh-century temple, 14 metre surviving height, Almaqah, Christian reuse, timber/masonry palace and collective shaft tombs possibly representing family groups.

Direct 9 September 2026 DAI report: horizontal timber and masonry, modelling of possible load capacity, actual height unknown and further geometry/floor modelling required. Public text does not convert theoretical capacity into built height.
Direct original research abstract: plant/animal fats, fruit fermentation markers, small serving pots and tentative moringa seed oil. Public text retains sample limits and uncertainty.

Direct original edition pages 17 to 18: bn / bn, translation son of the son, woman Taʿattarat and goddess. Source caveat about surviving thumbnail and lost documentation read. Unicode display is expressly normalized, not a facsimile.

Direct excavation abstract: trench from late second millennium BCE, first-half first-millennium occupation, second-half gap and later Aksumite reoccupation. Public text does not extrapolate a regional abandonment.

Direct critical edition: MRAC.STRO.1 author/date and Arabic opening with French translation, trade in animals, textiles, guns and enslaved people; MRAC.DHA.9 exact Roman transcription hao kila mtu kwa watu wake and French translation each is there for his men. Later authorship is carefully distinguished from ruler autographs.

Direct original article selected passages: subordinate local officials, provincial oversight, food crisis by 1898 and less devastated Gujba as grain source. Some PDF extracted lines are clipped; review limited to readable passages.

Direct primary chapter: post-conquest journey, rain-retaining channels, milk/butter, millet, timber-bundle palace supports and plaster. Public observations narrowly attributed to Gentil; hostile generalizations omitted. Market list not independently checked.
Direct original publisher extract: both leaders died in 1884, vatwale governors, changing alliance in 1880 and German dismantling in 1895.

Direct original study selected passages: distinct Unyanyembe/Itetemia/Tabora, conquest from 1893, stored grains, stockades, returning bush and tsetse. Other crop and campaign detail retains author review.
Direct original occupational discussion: wage renegotiation, multilingual kirangozi, food/water/tribute responsibilities and cloth/bead payments. Healing discussion not independently checked.

limits: Seven other sources not independently reopened; author access notes retained, including indexed-only sources.
Damot attribution remains an explicitly labelled inference from northern geometry and BCE dates; exact borders and lifetime are not certified.
Rabih’s eastern imported polygon is not presented as the extent of later Borno rule.
Composite Tanzanian record explicitly separates polities and their different endings.
